# mdread

> mdread is a free, open-source Markdown (MD) reader and viewer for Windows 10 and 11. It opens .md files instantly and renders GitHub-flavored Markdown (tables, task lists, footnotes, strikethrough, autolinks, alerts), with light/dark/system themes and live reload when the file changes. 1.5 MB installer or 4.9 MB portable exe; MIT license; no account or telemetry. Built with Rust (pulldown-cmark), Tauri 2 and the WebView2 runtime built into Windows.

Key facts:

- Name: mdread (repository: md-reader)
- Category: Markdown viewer / reader (read-only; not an editor)
- Platform: Windows 10 and Windows 11, x64
- Latest version: 0.1.0, released 2026-10-17
- Price: free; license: MIT
- Install: per-user installer (no admin rights) that registers .md, .markdown, .mdown, .mkd, .mkdn, or a portable single exe
- Open a file: double-click a .md file, drag it onto the window, `mdread.exe file.md`, or Ctrl+O
- Shortcuts: Ctrl+T theme, Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 text size, F5 reload, Alt+Left / Alt+Right back and forward through linked notes
- Safety: scripts embedded in Markdown never run; links to local non-Markdown files are revealed in Explorer, not executed
- Builds are not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run (More info, then Run anyway)
- When to use something else: for writing Markdown, an editor such as VS Code, Typora or Obsidian fits better; on Windows 11, Notepad can format basic Markdown while editing
